title: Average randomized complexity
statement: Let $f$ be a function on inputs of length $n$ over a finite alphabet, and let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on that alphabet. Its average randomized complexity is the infimum of the average costs, under independent sampling from $\pi$, of randomized decision trees that compute $f$ with zero error.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability distribution on the alphabet.
caveat: The supplied statement does not include the definition of input cost, so its precise cost convention cannot be specified.
